# **CINEC Campus Undergraduate, Foundation, Diploma, and HND Programme Audit**

## **Coverage Summary and Institutional Scope**

This audit compiles structured programme data for **CINEC Campus** (https\://www\.cinec.edu/) across its undergraduate degrees, foundation programmes, diplomas, and Higher National Diplomas (HNDs), excluding all postgraduate degrees (MSc, MBA, LLM, PhD) and short vocational, STCW maritime, or certificate courses1. Because CINEC Campus operates eight academic faculties alongside branch campuses in Nugegoda, Jaffna, and Trincomalee4, this report completes the full non-postgraduate portfolio for the **Faculty of Computing** (9 programmes found), the **Faculty of Management and Social Sciences** (11 programmes found), and the diploma portfolio of **CINEC Business School / Metro Campus – Nugegoda** (5 programmes found), while additionally documenting 9 programmes from the **Faculty of Engineering and Technology** for which complete course-level records were retrieved6.  
In total, **34 programmes found** are documented in Section A, while **46 additional discovered programmes** across the remaining faculties (Faculty of Engineering and Technology, Faculty of Health Sciences, Faculty of Humanities and Education, Faculty of Science, Faculty of Maritime Sciences, Faculty of Marine Engineering, and Department of Aviation) and regional branches are catalogued in Section C for subsequent research2. Actual academic programmes are counted separately from website filter directories—such as qualification-level search filters (EDEXCEL HND, EDhat, BCS HEQ, or GCE A/L entry-level landing pages)—and internal entry routes, such as Year 2 lateral exemptions or specialist HND tracks shared under a single programme page7.

## **B. Programme Notes, Entry Mechanics, and Documentation Anomalies**

### **1\. Fee Architecture, Installment Plans, and Upfront Discounts**

Across the audited faculties, CINEC Campus employs a bifurcated pricing disclosure model in which programmes partnered with UK awarding bodies (Anglia Ruskin University and Pearson BTEC) and the four-year local Network Security degree publish explicit fee schedules online, whereas all Faculty of Management and Social Sciences programmes, University of Wolverhampton programmes, and Nugegoda Metro Campus diplomas omit online fee figures and require direct institutional inquiry6. Where fees are published, transnational programmes separate local tuition and registration charges (denominated in LKR) from annual partner university royalty fees (denominated in GBP)7.  
![][image1]  
An analysis of the installment schedules across the thirteen fee-disclosing programmes indicates that annual and semester payment plans consistently equal the stated whole-programme base tuition fee, whereas extended monthly or quarterly plans on engineering and four-year local degrees incorporate an administrative installment surcharge. Specifically, for the three-year Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) computing degrees (BSc (Hons) Computer Science, BSc (Hons) Software Engineering, and BSc (Hons) Artificial Intelligence) and the one-year BSc (Hons) Applied Computer Science (TopUp), the annual, semester, and monthly payment plans all sum exactly to the stated base course fee of LKR 1,200,000 (400,000 x 3, 200,000 x 6, or 40,000 x 30\) and LKR 400,000 (200,000 x 2 or 50,000 x 8), respectively15. By contrast, for the one-year ARU Engineering Level 6 Top-Up degrees (Civil, Mechanical, and Mechatronic), the single-payment (700,000 x 1\) and two-installment (350,000 x 2\) options match the LKR 700,000 base fee, while the four-installment plan (180,000 x 4\) totals LKR 720,00030. Similarly, for the three-year ARU BEng degrees (Civil, Automotive, Mechanical, and Electronic and Electrical), the annual (750,000 x 3\) and semester (375,000 x 6\) options match the LKR 2,250,000 base fee, whereas the 30-month plan (79,000 x 30\) carries an installment premium7. For the four-year local BSc (Hons) in Computer Science in Network Security and Forensics, the annual (525,000 x 4\) and semester (262,500 x 8\) plans match the LKR 2,100,000 base course fee, whereas the 46-month plan (46,000 x 46\) equals LKR 2,116,0009.  
Upfront payment discounts are explicitly structured across the engineering portfolio. On the three-year ARU BEng programmes (Civil, Mechanical, and Electronic and Electrical), CINEC offers tiered upfront payment reductions of 5% for paying the annual course fee upfront, 6% for paying two years' course fees upfront, and 7.5% for paying all three years' course fees upfront7. The PEARSON BTEC HND in Mechanical Engineering offers a 5% discount for one year paid upfront and 6% for two years paid upfront33. Within the Faculty of Computing, the ARU degrees and the local Network Security degree state that Open Day discounts are available, and the BSc (Hons) Applied Computer Science (TopUp) additionally notes a dedicated discount for internal CINEC HND students progressing to Level 69. Separately from degree tuition, CINEC publishes a USD fee schedule on its CDMP Payment Portal (https\://www\.cinec.edu/cdmp-payment-details.html) for standalone non-degree-seeking general education modules (PHYS-101 General Physics with Lab, CHEM-103 General Chemistry with Lab, GEN-105 Genetics, ENG-102 English with Composition, and STATS-104 Introduction to Statistics), each priced at USD 275 Course Fee plus USD 6 STAX, totaling USD 281 per module2.

### **2\. Entry Requirement Nuances, Bridging Routes, and Transfer Pathways**

Entry thresholds across the Faculty of Computing vary substantially depending on whether the qualification is awarded locally by CINEC, transnationally by Anglia Ruskin University (ARU), or transnationally by the University of Wolverhampton. The three ARU-awarded three-year degrees (Computer Science, Software Engineering, and Artificial Intelligence) accept 3 Simple ("S") passes at the Sri Lankan GCE A/L in any subject stream (or 3 "D" passes at London A/L, or the CINEC STEM Foundation Programme), paired with an English language requirement of at least Grade "C" at GCE O/L or Grade "S" in GCE A/L General English9. In contrast, the University of Wolverhampton BSc (Hons) Computer Science (Software Engineering) enforces a higher grade profile of 1 "C" and 2 "S" passes at Local GCE A/L (or 1 "C" and 2 "D" passes at London A/L) in any stream, alongside 5 Credit ("C") passes at GCE O/L that must specifically include Mathematics, Science, and English9.  
For CINEC's four-year local computing degrees (BSc (Hons) in Computer Science in Network Security and Forensics and BSc (Hons) in Software Engineering), direct entry without a bridging course is restricted to candidates holding 3 "S" passes in the Physical Science stream (or the Engineering Technology stream for Network Security) obtained in a single sitting9. Candidates with 3 "S" passes in any other GCE A/L stream must complete a mandatory bridging programme; for Network Security, non-Physical Science candidates must also hold a Credit ("C") pass in GCE O/L Mathematics, although the bridging requirement is waived if the applicant achieved at least a Simple ("S") pass in GCE A/L Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in any sitting9. A comparable bridging mechanism applies to Engineering Technology stream applicants for the PEARSON BTEC HND in Mechanical Engineering, who must hold at least 2 "C" passes and 1 "S" pass at GCE A/L (meeting a minimum 5-point threshold) and complete an engineering bridging programme33.  
Lateral entry and international transfer rules also diverge between computing and engineering. The three-year ARU Computing degrees and the four-year local Network Security degree explicitly prohibit lateral entry at Year 2 or Year 3 (Exemptions: N/A – No lateral Entries available at any level)9. Instead, computing diploma and HND holders are directed into the one-year BSc (Hons) Applied Computer Science (TopUp) at Level 69. Conversely, the three-year ARU BEng degrees (Civil, Automotive, and Mechanical) permit direct Second Year (Level 5\) entry for applicants holding an appropriate HNC/HND or City & Guilds Advanced Technician Diploma7, while Pearson BTEC HND Engineering graduates may also progress directly into the third year (Level 6 Top-Up) of a UK partner BEng programme31. Both the ARU Computing degrees and the ARU Civil Engineering degree state that students have the option to transfer to the UK at the end of Year 1 or Year 2 to complete their degree on campus in the United Kingdom7.
